title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The notes build, for each 'MD-graph' G (a stable graph of a pants/Lego decomposition), a groupoid S_0T_G: the level-0 piece of the Teichmüller tower attached to G. On the previous page Grothendieck gave an intrinsic description when G has modular dimension 0 (formula (28)). Objects are the elements of a torsor E(G). Morphisms x→y are the fibre over y−x ∈ γ(G) of an extension of γ(G) by a lattice. Composition is addition. He now works out the first nontrivial example: the type (0,4) graph with one edge, two trivalent vertices, each vertex carrying two free legs.

The square. The data is a 4-element set I with a partition of type (2,2). Grothendieck packages it as a 'combinatorial square' Q with vertex set I, whose two diagonals are the two blocks of the partition.
- diag Q is the set of the two diagonals.
- A(Q) is the set of the four sides. A side is exactly a choice of one vertex on each diagonal, so A(Q) = ∏_{Δ∈diag Q} Δ. This is a torsor under {±1}^{diag Q}.
- The diagonal subgroup {±1} acts by swapping both endpoints, i.e. sending a side to the opposite side.
- The quotient pairs opposite sides; these pairs are the 'codiagonals'. So codiag(Q) = A(Q)/{±1} = ∧_{Δ} Δ, the contracted product of the two 2-element sets.
- In modern terms: of the three (2,2)-partitions of I, one is the given one; the two others are indexed by codiag(Q).

Dictionary with the graph G_Q.
- Vertex set S ≅ diag Q; vertex s carries the free legs Δ_s.
- I = A^lib, the free half-edges, i.e. the vertices of Q.
- Half-edges: Â = I ⊔ S̃, where s̃ is the half of the internal edge with origin s.
- At each vertex, Â_s = Δ_s ⊔ {s̃} has three elements.
- E_s = co(Â_s) is the set of cyclic orders on Â_s. It is identified with Δ_s via 'the successor of s̃'; it is a {±1}-torsor.
- Hence E(G) = ∏_s Δ_s ≅ A(Q). Choosing cyclic orders (ribbon structures) at both pants is the same as choosing a side of the square.
- γ(G) = {±1}^S.

The groupoid. Push the γ(G)-torsor E(G) along the extension 0→Z^S --2--> Z^S → {±1}^S → 0. This gives a Z^S-torsor over the γ(G)-torsor, hence S_0T_G: 4 objects (the sides), with Hom(x,y) the parity class of Z^S over y−x.
- Geometrically, a generator of Z^S at s is a half-twist of pants s. It reverses the cyclic order, i.e. passes to an adjacent side of Q.
- Its square is the 'full rotation' of the pants.

Next page. The full-rotation sublattice Z^S is mapped into the twist lattice Z^Â = Z^I × Z. This map is the transpose of the origin map on oriented half-edges, followed by covariance along the quotient by the involution.
- It splits as Z^S → Z^I, the transpose of the degree-2 map I→S.
- And Z^S → Z, summation. Both ends of the edge contribute to the single edge twist.
- This is the combinatorial form of the relation σ² = twist(outer) · twist(leg 1)^{-1} · twist(leg 2)^{-1} (signs and framing aside). In ribbon-category language it is the balancing axiom θ_{a⊗b} = c_{b,a}c_{a,b}(θ_a⊗θ_b).
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. The construction is coherent: A(Q)=∏Δ_s is a genuine torsor, its quotient by the diagonal {±1} is the codiagonal set, and E(G)≅A(Q) is correct via 'successor of s̃' in the cyclic order.
Minor: the notation for the group alternates between γ(G)/γ_G (and δ(G) on the previous page). The meaning of the map 'Z^S · Z^Â' is only clarified on the next page, and the sentence is cut off.

ideas.what: Model the (0,4) one-edge stable graph as a 'combinatorial square'. Diagonals are the given (2,2)-partition, sides are ∏Δ, codiagonals are the other two (2,2)-partitions; codiag(Q)=∧Δ.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorics of the three pants decompositions of S_{0,4} / cross-ratio symmetric group action (Klein four-group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; used in Hatcher–Thurston and in Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps for the (0,4) 'Lego' piece
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the (0,4) and (1,1) generators of the Teichmüller tower but not this square formalism explicitly

ideas.what: Objects of the level-0 Teichmüller groupoid of a graph form a torsor E(G)=∏ co(Â_s) of cyclic orders at vertices, i.e. ribbon-graph structures.
ideas.modern_name: Ribbon (fat) graph structures / orientations of pants as objects of the Moore–Seiberg / Bakalov–Kirillov Lego–Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2 (Teichmüller tower) in spirit

ideas.what: S_0T_G for modular dimension 0 as the pushout of a γ(G)-torsor along 0→Z^S→Z^S→{±1}^S→0, i.e. a half-twist groupoid. The full rotations map to boundary/edge twists by the 'transpose of origin' map, giving the balancing relation.
ideas.modern_name: Half-twist (braiding) groupoid; balancing axiom of ribbon categories; boundary twist relation in the pure mapping class group of pants

missed.claim: This is an explicit worked example of an intrinsic, torsor-theoretic description of the level-0 Teichmüller groupoid attached to a stable graph. Objects are ribbon structures and morphisms are lattice cosets. Contents equivalent to the (0,3)/(0,4) part of the Bakalov–Kirillov Lego–Teichmüller groupoid appear later in the literature, but this functorial formulation (pushout of the γ(G)-torsor along the multiplication-by-2 extension) is not, to my knowledge, published as such.
missed.quote: On trouve S_0 T_G à l'aide de l'extension 0 → Z^S →2 Z^S → {±1}^S → 0 et du γ(G)-torseur (E(G))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck worked out the combinatorics of the Teichmüller tower in a canonical, coordinate-free form. This is relevant to Grothendieck–Teichmüller and Lego-Teichmüller groupoid work, but it is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, canonical but elementary worked example (square ↔ (0,4) graph, sides = products of diagonals, half-twist groupoid). It is consistent with later Lego-Teichmüller formalisms and contains no result unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'I = A^lib = [-S-](Q) ens des [-côtés-] {+sommets+} de Q': the overwritten symbol is a struck-out letter, and the meaning is the set of vertices (sommets) of Q. Confidence is moderate.
'Â ≃ I ⊔ S̃ ens associé à s∈S l'arête orientée liée de l'origine s' is better read as 'S̃ ensemble associé : s∈S ↦ l'arête orientée liée d'origine s'.
'E(G) ≃ ∏Δ_s ≃ A(Q) ens torsor [?] sous [?]' reads 'ensemble torseur sous γ(G)'.
'E_{Gb}' is probably 'E_G^b' (the extension attached to G), written with a superscript.
'induit Z^S · Z^Â' should be read as a map Z^S → Z^Â, as confirmed by the next page.
The marginal addition 'qui donne un Z^S-torseur sur γ(G)' should be read as 'un Z^S-torseur sur E(G)' / over the γ(G)-torsor.
